newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers Cantel, AT&T Canada form alliance.
newsitem.headline: Rogers Cantel, AT&T Canada form alliance.

text.p: Canadian wireless telephone provider Rogers Cantel Mobile Communications Inc. and AT&T' Corp.'s Canadian unit forged an alliance Wednesday that includes the licensing of AT&T brands to Cantel.

The deal also includes a technology and marketing pact with AT&T Wireless Services, including AT&T's digital personal communications services (PCS). Cantel last week launched its own PCS services, which offer customers wireless access via portable digital telephones.
Executives from both companies, including AT&T Chairman Bob Allen, called the deal a "win-win" agreement.
"The alliance that we are now seeing is a clear demonstration of our commitment to the Canadian market," Allen told reporters and industry analysts.
AT&T, the largest U.S. long-distance phone company, already owns 33 percent of AT&T Canada Long Distance Services, formerly Unitel Communications Inc., one of Canada's biggest long-distance carriers.

Cantel, Canada's largest cellular phone network, gets use of the AT&T brand and will market wireless products and services under the Cantel AT&T name. The companies will combine market research and share development costs.

Cantel Chief Executive Stanley Kabala, who worked at AT&T for about 14 years, said the combination will place 8.5 million cellular customers under one umbrella, offering them "seamless" services on both sides of the U.S.-Canada border such as messaging and network access codes.
"We certainly expect revenues to rise and margins to improve. We expect to see customers attracted to the power of this co-brand that we have in the marketplace," Kabala said.

The companies said the agreement involves royalty payments, the issue of Cantel warrants and payments to AT&T for marketing and technical support. The warrants are exchangeable for as much as C$32.5 million ($24.4 million) worth of Cantel class B shares.

Media reports this month had speculated that the two companies would sign a deal in which AT&T Canada would get a significant chunk of Cantel's equity. Cantel Chairman Ted Rogers denied the report at the time.
Phil Lind, Rogers Communications Inc. vice-chairman, said the warrants represent less than 1 percent of Cantel's outstanding stock. Rogers Communications owns 97.6 percent of Cantel.
Neither company ruled out an eventual equity investment.

"As people work together, there are always opportunities for investment if that's in the interests of both parties. But that has not been something that I wish to discuss at this time," Ted Rogers told the briefing.
But there is no standstill agreement in the pact to prevent AT&T from ultimately taking a stake in Cantel.
